paragraphs: This paper studies sparse regression across multiple computing agents when the number of parameters can exceed, and grow faster than, the number of samples. Existing accelerated distributed methods can perform poorly in this setting. The aim is to obtain the benefits of acceleration while respecting both the statistical difficulty of high dimensions and the need for communication.

The proposed algorithm combines accelerated proximal gradient updates with consensus and gradient tracking. Consensus encourages agents to agree on their estimates, while gradient tracking lets each agent maintain a local estimate of the empirical loss gradient. These mechanisms connect progress at individual agents to progress on the shared estimation problem.

Under stated assumptions on the statistical model and tuning parameters, the method converges globally at a linear rate to within the model's statistical precision. Its iteration complexity scales with the square root of the restricted condition number, while communication depends on network connectivity and agent count. The authors also derive an accelerated method for master-worker systems.
neurips-2022-acceleration-in-distributed.tldr: A distributed sparse-regression algorithm achieves accelerated convergence to statistical precision under stated model and tuning assumptions.

paragraphs: Sliced Wasserstein methods compare probability distributions through projections, but the choice of projection direction matters. Finding informative directions typically requires iterative optimization. In deep learning, this search must be repeated as new pairs of mini-batches are compared, creating an expensive optimization loop inside the larger model-training loop.

The paper proposes learning to predict useful directions directly from the two mini-batch distributions. This is amortized optimization: a learned model takes on a task that would otherwise require repeated optimization for each input. The purpose is to make informative projections more practical when distribution comparisons occur many times during training.

The authors develop linear, generalized linear, and nonlinear versions of these predictors, producing three corresponding mini-batch losses called amortized sliced Wasserstein losses. They report favorable performance for deep generative modeling on standard benchmarks. The contribution connects the quality of projection-based comparisons with the cost of obtaining those projections, making direction selection itself a learned component of the training approach.
neurips-2022-amortized-projection-optimi.tldr: Learned projection predictors replace repeated direction optimization to make sliced Wasserstein losses more practical for generative modeling.

paragraphs: BadPrompt investigates backdoor vulnerabilities in continuous prompt learning, a setting where prompts steer a model toward downstream language tasks. The authors focus on few-shot learning, where limited training examples make existing language-model backdoor methods difficult to apply. Their question is whether an attack adapted to prompt learning can remain effective in this setting.

The proposed method has two stages. It first identifies candidate triggers associated with the attacker's target label and dissimilar to examples carrying other labels. It then uses adaptive optimization to select a trigger for each sample, seeking both attack effectiveness and low visibility. This makes trigger selection responsive to the task and individual examples.

Experiments cover five datasets and two continuous prompt models. The authors report effective attacks, large improvements over the evaluated baselines, and continued high performance on clean test data. That combination is the central security finding: successful behavior on ordinary examples can coexist with a backdoor in the evaluated prompt-based models.
neurips-2022-badprompt-backdoor-attacks-.tldr: BadPrompt demonstrates effective backdoor attacks on continuous prompts while preserving high performance on clean test examples.

paragraphs: DART expands a widely used hand model to represent more of the appearance variation found in hand images. The underlying MANO model does not include textures or accessories, which limits its ability to produce photorealistic training data. DART adds these ingredients while retaining an articulated hand representation.

The resource includes 50 everyday three-dimensional accessories and 325 manually created texture maps covering variations such as blemishes and makeup. A Unity interface lets users configure pose, camera, background, lighting, textures, and accessories. These controls allow synthetic examples to vary in appearance as well as hand configuration.

The authors also release DARTset, containing 800,000 synthetic hand images paired with aligned three-dimensional labels. Their experiments report greater diversity and improved generalization for hand pose estimation and mesh recovery when DARTset complements existing datasets. The contribution combines a configurable generation tool with a large labeled dataset, linking richer visual variation to improvements in the evaluated hand-understanding tasks.
neurips-2022-dart-articulated-hand-model.tldr: DART adds textures and accessories to hand modeling and provides synthetic data that improves generalization in evaluated hand reconstruction tasks.

paragraphs: DeVRF addresses the long training times of radiance-field methods for synthesizing new views of moving, deformable scenes. Its representation stores both a reference three-dimensional scene and a deformation field in explicit voxel grids. The deformation field describes changes across space and time, connecting the reference scene to its changing appearance.

These grids contain many parameters and can overfit. The authors therefore introduce a static-to-dynamic training procedure alongside a practical capture setup. They first learn the reference volume from static images taken from multiple viewpoints, then use that learned structure to support deformation learning from dynamic sequences with only a few viewpoints.

Additional strategies refine efficiency and synthesized image quality. Evaluations on synthetic and real scenes with different deformations report a 100-fold speedup over previous state-of-the-art approaches while maintaining comparable visual fidelity. The result shows how explicit representations and a staged capture-and-learning procedure can work together to make dynamic scene reconstruction substantially faster in the tested settings.
neurips-2022-devrf-fast-deformable-voxel.tldr: DeVRF combines voxel representations with static-to-dynamic learning to report 100-fold faster dynamic radiance-field training at comparable visual fidelity.

paragraphs: This paper connects the geometry of the optimal receiver operating characteristic curve to a mathematical measure of distributional difference. It shows that the curve's arc length is an f-divergence. This gives a way to study an optimal classification curve through samples from the positive and negative classes.

Using that connection, the authors express arc length as a variational objective and construct an estimator. They establish a nonparametric convergence rate of O_p(n^(-β/4)), where β lies between zero and one and depends on smoothness. The guarantee therefore links estimation accuracy to both sample size and the smoothness governing the problem.

A related variational construction describes the area between the optimal curve and the diagonal. This leads to a two-step classification procedure that maximizes an approximate lower bound on the largest achievable area under the curve. Experiments on imbalanced binary tasks using CIFAR-10 report good AUC performance. The practical procedure thus follows from the paper's geometric and statistical characterization, without claiming to maximize the exact optimal AUC.
neurips-2022-estimating-the-arc-length-o.tldr: A divergence interpretation of optimal ROC geometry yields an arc-length estimator and a classifier that optimizes an approximate lower bound on maximal AUC.

paragraphs: Learning from very long sequences can require remembering events far in the past. Standard gradient-based training stores intermediate computations along the sequence, which becomes prohibitively expensive for sequences containing thousands or millions of elements. The difficulty is therefore partly about the memory needed to train the model.

MemUP builds on the observation that local context usually suffices for many sequence predictions. Predictions that depend on distant events are comparatively sparse and remain uncertain when only nearby information is available. The method uses this connection between uncertainty and long-term dependence to learn without backpropagating through an entire sequence at once.

The authors report that an LSTM trained with MemUP matches or exceeds the evaluated baselines while storing less intermediate data. This supports uncertainty-guided training as a way to make long-term memory learning more economical. They also describe potential applicability to any recurrent architecture; that broader possibility is distinct from the reported LSTM result.
neurips-2022-explain-my-surprise-learnin.tldr: MemUP uses locally uncertain predictions to guide long-term memory learning while reducing stored training intermediates in reported LSTM experiments.

paragraphs: FIRE explores how word representations can express multiple meanings. The paper argues that conventional linear vector spaces do not easily capture the nonlinearity needed for polysemy. It proposes a semantic field in which each word is described by multiple locations together with a nonlinear function spread across that field.

A function value at a particular location measures the strength of a word's relationship to another word there. Multiple locations and multiple peaks in the function represent different senses. Combining meanings is handled through addition of functions, giving the representation an explicit mechanism for both polysemy and composition.

The authors implement FIRE for English and evaluate word and sentence similarity, reporting comparable or better results than earlier representation methods. In a task that predicts how many senses a word has, FIRE substantially outperforms BERT and Word2vec. This result provides evidence that the field representation captures information about multiple meanings, alongside its reported usefulness for similarity judgments.
neurips-2022-fire-semantic-field-of-word.tldr: FIRE represents words as nonlinear semantic fields and reports strong results for predicting how many meanings a word has.

paragraphs: GAMA studies adversarial attacks on scenes containing several prominent objects. Many previous attack methods focus on images dominated by one object, while natural scenes contain objects whose meanings are related. The paper asks how those relationships can inform perturbations that transfer to unfamiliar classifiers.

The method uses the pretrained vision-language model CLIP to incorporate information from both images and language when training a perturbation generator. Joint image-text features supply semantic context about the scene's objects. This places relationships between objects within the generator's training signal, extending the attack approach beyond a single dominant subject.

The authors report effective transferable perturbations across several attack settings. In a black-box setting where both the attacker's classifier architecture and data distribution differ from the victim's, GAMA produces approximately 16% more misclassification than the compared state-of-the-art generative methods. These findings demonstrate that the semantic information available in a vision-language model can strengthen attacks on the evaluated multi-object scenes.
neurips-2022-gama-generative-adversarial.tldr: GAMA uses CLIP's image-text features to train transferable adversarial perturbations for scenes containing multiple related objects.

paragraphs: GT-GAN addresses the generation of synthetic time series, which can be used for data augmentation. The paper distinguishes regular and irregular time series and identifies a practical gap: existing generators had not shown good performance on both types without changes to the model. Its objective is a single framework that handles both.

The proposed approach is based on a generative adversarial network and integrates techniques for modeling time continuously. These include neural ordinary differential equations, neural controlled differential equations, and continuous time-flow processes. Combining them within one framework is central to the proposal, because the intended capability spans both regular and irregular observations.

The authors describe GT-GAN as a general-purpose synthesis model and report that it outperforms existing methods. The significance of this claim lies in the shared model across the two time-series categories: the framework is intended to avoid requiring a different model design for each. The paper's stated contribution therefore combines broader applicability within time-series synthesis with reported performance improvements.
neurips-2022-gt-gan-general-purpose-time.tldr: GT-GAN combines adversarial learning with continuous-time modeling to synthesize both regular and irregular time series using one framework.

paragraphs: This paper investigates how agents in a shared task can learn different behaviors through skills. Heterogeneous behavior is common in multi-agent problems, yet the authors argue that automatically identifying and representing it has received insufficient attention. Their framework makes skill discovery, assignment, and policy learning explicit parts of training.

An autoencoder uses environmental information to produce latent skill representations. These representations help distinguish agents for skill assignment and distinguish skills during learning. A selector assigns skills to agents, while a separate learning mechanism produces policies associated with those skills. A mutual-information-based intrinsic reward encourages efficient discovery of diverse skills.

The framework is evaluated on StarCraft II micromanagement, Google Research Football, and GoBigger. The authors report the best performance among the compared state-of-the-art multi-agent reinforcement learning methods on these benchmarks. The results support treating behavioral diversity as something to represent and organize directly, with learned skills connecting the agents' differences to their task performance.
neurips-2022-heterogeneous-skill-learnin.tldr: A multi-agent framework learns, assigns, and rewards diverse skills, reporting leading performance on three evaluated benchmarks.

paragraphs: This paper proposes hiding a secret image inside a learned probabilistic model. Conventional neural approaches use an encoder to place a message into a carrier and a decoder to retrieve it. Here, the hiding location is a particular point within the distribution learned by a generative model.

The authors instantiate the idea with SinGAN, a pyramid of generative adversarial networks that learns the patch distribution of one cover image. During that learning process, they also fit a deterministic mapping from a fixed collection of noise maps to the secret image. An embedding key generates those noise maps and therefore provides the means of recovering the hidden content.

The resulting model is publicly communicated while retaining the behavior of the original SinGAN; the intended receiver uses the key to extract the image. The authors demonstrate feasibility in extraction accuracy and model security. They also show that the approach can accommodate multiple secret images for different receivers and can obfuscate a secret image.
neurips-2022-hiding-images-in-deep-proba.tldr: A SinGAN-based framework hides images at keyed locations in a learned generative distribution and demonstrates their recovery.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning builds policies from previously collected data without requesting new environmental interactions. LAPO targets datasets assembled from different demonstrators or policies, which can contain several distinct patterns of action. Such datasets may also include too few high-reward trajectories, making policy learning difficult.

The method uses a latent-variable generative model to represent state-action pairs with high advantage. This emphasizes parts of the observed behavior that contribute to solving the task while accommodating varied action patterns. A policy operating over the latent variable then seeks higher rewards through that representation.

The authors evaluate LAPO on simulated locomotion, navigation, and manipulation tasks. They report average performance improvements over the next best-performing offline methods of 49% on heterogeneous datasets and 8% on datasets with narrow, biased distributions. These results support the proposed combination of expressive action modeling and advantage-based emphasis in the evaluated settings. The reported gains concern learning from existing datasets, consistent with the method's offline objective.
neurips-2022-lapo-latent-variable-advant.tldr: LAPO uses an advantage-weighted latent action model to improve offline policy learning, especially on the evaluated heterogeneous datasets.

paragraphs: Spatially adaptive networks save computation by spending more effort on informative image regions. However, fewer mathematical operations do not automatically produce faster execution, especially on multicore hardware. This paper addresses the gap between computational savings and actual latency by incorporating scheduling and hardware behavior into network design.

LASNet performs coarse-grained spatial adaptation under the guidance of a latency predictor. The predictor considers the algorithm, its scheduling strategy, and the hardware on which it runs. The authors use its estimates to guide both architectural decisions and scheduling optimization across different platforms.

Experiments on classification, object detection, and instance segmentation report improved practical inference efficiency. For ResNet-101 on ImageNet validation data, average latency falls by 36% on a Tesla V100 and 46% on a Jetson TX2 GPU without an accuracy reduction. These examples show the value of optimizing predicted runtime alongside adaptive computation: the reported benefit is measured execution speed on particular devices, rather than operation-count savings alone.
neurips-2022-latency-aware-spatial-wise-.tldr: LASNet uses hardware- and scheduling-aware latency prediction to turn spatially adaptive computation into measured inference speedups.

paragraphs: This paper tackles the separation of individual objects in three-dimensional point clouds, where complex local geometry makes boundaries difficult to identify. It first divides the point cloud into small regions called superpoints and connects them in a graph. The remaining problem is to determine which connected regions belong together.

An edge prediction network learns relationships between neighboring superpoints using attention in both coordinate space and learned feature space. A geometry-aware training loss encourages neighboring regions from the same object to align with that object's center in both spaces. This ties the predicted connections to the structure of individual objects.

A graph-cut network then combines these edge scores with predicted semantic classes to produce object instances. Its bilateral attention mechanism draws on coordinates and features when predicting labels and instance scores. Experiments on ScanNet v2 and S3DIS report new state-of-the-art results. The approach makes local geometric relationships a learned ingredient throughout grouping, from evaluating neighboring regions to assembling complete instances.
neurips-2022-learning-superpoint-graph-c.tldr: A learned superpoint graph-cut method combines geometric relationships and semantic predictions to separate individual objects in point clouds.

paragraphs: This paper studies policy evaluation when the value of an intervention emerges through a downstream optimization problem. In applications involving matching, assignment, or network flow, operational restrictions mean that averaging individual causal outcomes does not capture the decision-maker's utility. The relevant outcome depends on how those effects change a later decision.

The proposed framework handles policy-dependent linear optimization responses, with causal outcomes making the objective coefficients stochastic. This introduces optimization bias even when the task is only to evaluate a policy. The paper therefore treats the optimization response as part of the quantity being estimated, rather than stopping at individual outcomes.

The authors construct unbiased estimators using perturbations and analyze asymptotic variance properties for adjusted plug-in estimators. They also provide a general algorithm for optimizing causal interventions once unbiased policy evaluation is available. Numerical simulations corroborate the theoretical findings. The contribution links causal evaluation to the operational decision that ultimately determines utility, within the specified linear optimization framework.
neurips-2022-off-policy-evaluation-with-.tldr: A causal policy-evaluation framework accounts for downstream linear optimization and uses perturbations to construct unbiased value estimators.

paragraphs: This paper examines what gradient-based training implicitly favors in neural networks. Prior theory for homogeneous networks trained with exponential or logistic loss connects gradient flow to a Karush–Kuhn–Tucker point of a parameter-space maximum-margin problem. The unresolved issue is whether reaching such a point also means reaching an actual optimum.

The authors investigate this distinction across several architectures using linear and ReLU activations. They show that, in many cases, the point reached is not even a local optimum of the margin objective. Thus, the previously established optimization conditions alone do not justify concluding that training maximizes the margin.

The paper also identifies multiple settings in which local or global optimality can be guaranteed. Its contribution is therefore a more precise account of when margin-maximization interpretations are valid. The negative results separate convergence to a qualifying stationary point from true optimization, while the positive results establish circumstances where the stronger conclusion is supported.
neurips-2022-on-margin-maximization-in-l.tldr: Gradient-flow convergence to a maximum-margin KKT point need not yield even a local optimum, though some settings admit stronger guarantees.

paragraphs: PDSketch combines human-specified structure, learned transition models, and online planning for robotics. It focuses on locality and sparsity in how an environment changes: which objects and features depend on which others. The goal is to use that structure to support generalization and improve the efficiency of learning and planning.

The proposed domain language lets users describe high-level dependencies while neural networks learn the remaining details of environmental transitions. This gives programmers a way to express structural knowledge without manually specifying every part of the transition model. The abstract compares that role to choosing architectural structure when defining a neural network.

From the specified structure and learned parameters, PDSketch automatically produces domain-independent planning heuristics. These heuristics require no additional training and accelerate planning for new goals at execution time. The contribution connects the model's programmed structure to its later use in planning, allowing the same structural description to guide both learning environmental behavior and searching for actions.
neurips-2022-pdsketch-integrated-domain-.tldr: PDSketch combines programmed transition structure with neural learning and automatically derived heuristics to accelerate planning for novel goals.

paragraphs: Polyhistor studies how to adapt pretrained vision models to several dense prediction tasks while training relatively few parameters. Keeping a separately fine-tuned model for every task is inefficient. The authors also find that methods developed for language Transformers do not integrate efficiently with the hierarchical structure of the vision Transformers they study.

The paper first benchmarks parameter-efficient methods in single-task and multitask settings across four dense vision tasks. It then introduces Polyhistor and Polyhistor-Lite, using decomposed hypernetworks and layer-wise scaling kernels. These components support information sharing across tasks while keeping the number of trainable parameters small.

The authors report favorable performance relative to existing parameter-efficient methods with fewer trainable parameters. Polyhistor achieves accuracy competitive with the state of the art using less than 10% of the compared methods' trainable parameters. Gains are larger with bigger networks and more pretraining data. The findings connect efficient adaptation to the hierarchical architecture and multitask setting in which it must operate.
neurips-2022-polyhistor-parameter-effici.tldr: Polyhistor shares adaptation across dense vision tasks, achieving competitive accuracy with less than 10% of the compared state-of-the-art methods' trainable parameters.

paragraphs: A label distribution describes degrees of relevance across labels, offering richer information than simple yes-or-no assignments. Directly collecting these distributions is costly, while reconstructing them from logical labels can be unstable. This paper investigates ranked labels as an intermediate form of annotation that balances information and annotation effort.

The authors theoretically relate a ranking to the distributions it can represent. They define expected approximation error to measure annotation quality, derive bounds for rankings, and identify an optimal range of distributions corresponding to a given ranking. This analysis characterizes what information ranked annotations can provide about label relevance.

The proposed learning framework uses conditional Dirichlet mixtures to recover distributions from rankings while learning to predict them end to end. A scoring function allows task knowledge to enter the process. Extensive experiments validate the proposal. The contribution brings together a theoretical account of ranking quality and a practical method for turning that form of supervision into distributional predictions.
neurips-2022-predicting-label-distributi.tldr: The paper uses ranked labels as intermediate supervision for learning label distributions, supported by approximation bounds and an end-to-end mixture model.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether one embodied agent can handle navigation goals expressed in different ways. Existing specialized agents address individual tasks such as navigating toward an image, an object, a sound, or a language-described goal. The authors introduce VXN, a large-scale dataset bringing four navigation tasks into standardized continuous environments with audiovisual information.

Their agent, Vienna, uses one attention-based model for all four tasks. It interprets a target description together with task embeddings into several goal vectors. As navigation proceeds, it refines these vectors and uses them to query the episode's history for information that supports the next decision.

This shared procedure lets knowledge be reused across tasks with different input modalities. Empirical comparisons show that the multitask agent achieves performance comparable to or better than learning the tasks individually, with reduced complexity. The contribution combines a common evaluation environment with a common decision-making architecture, demonstrating the feasibility of sharing navigation capabilities across the four studied tasks.
neurips-2022-towards-versatile-embodied-.tldr: Vienna handles four navigation tasks with one model, matching or improving on separate task learning while reducing complexity.

paragraphs: This paper analyzes stochastic gradient descent with momentum for least squares when both sample count and dimension are large. It studies how batch size affects the benefit of momentum. As dimension increases, the training dynamics converge to a deterministic discrete Volterra equation, providing a mathematical description of the optimization trajectory.

The analysis identifies a stability quantity called the implicit conditioning ratio. When batch size exceeds this ratio, the method achieves a linear convergence rate with O(1/√κ) dependence, matching optimal full-batch momentum. In this regime, a batch containing only a fraction of the data can provide the same convergence performance as a full batch.

Below that threshold, convergence rates instead scale as a multiple of the single-batch SGD rate. The authors also give explicit learning-rate and momentum choices based on the Hessian spectrum. These results explain a batch-size boundary for acceleration in the studied high-dimensional least-squares setting and connect parameter selection to the problem's curvature.
neurips-2022-trajectory-of-mini-batch-mo.tldr: For high-dimensional least squares, an implicit conditioning ratio identifies when mini-batch momentum can match full-batch convergence.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether a Transformer's forward computation can be understood as steps that reduce an underlying energy function. Such an interpretation would connect the architecture to an explicit optimization process. The motivation is to provide a mathematical perspective complementary to the heuristics and experience commonly used in model design.

The authors investigate obstacles to extending this perspective to self-attention. Related interpretations exist for simpler architectures, but the complexity of attention makes the correspondence harder to establish. They outline the main difficulties and introduce techniques that address them at least partially.

The result is a close association between energy minimization and deep layers containing self-attention. The abstract presents this as progress toward an optimization interpretation, rather than a complete resolution of every obstacle for Transformers. Its significance is explanatory: viewing successive computations as an unfolding optimization process can sharpen intuition about the model. The authors also identify possible value for future architectures, without claiming that new designs are already established by this analysis.
neurips-2022-transformers-from-an-optimi.tldr: The paper establishes a close connection between self-attention layers and energy minimization while partially addressing obstacles to an optimization interpretation of Transformers.

paragraphs: This paper develops unsupervised scene understanding around a model of how cameras form images of three-dimensional objects. Its representation describes object shapes, colors, and positions, with each object stored as a separate neural radiance field placed in a scene. Training reconstructs images observed from multiple viewpoints.

The authors then introduce an inference procedure that recovers this scene representation from a single image outside the training distribution. The studied changes include unseen combinations of components, new spatial arrangements, and substantially different viewpoints. Separating objects and their placement allows the model to express these changes within its generative account of image formation.

Experiments use test datasets assigned zero probability by the training distribution. The authors report accurate geometry reconstruction, object segmentation, and position inference without supervision, along with substantial improvements over baselines that do not model the causal image-generation process. The findings support explicit object-based image formation as a useful basis for generalization under the distribution shifts examined.
neurips-2022-unsupervised-causal-generat.tldr: An object-based causal image generator learns from multiple views and reconstructs scenes from single images under the evaluated out-of-distribution shifts.

paragraphs: ViewFool evaluates how recognition models respond when a real object is viewed from difficult camera positions. This extends robustness testing beyond transformations of a two-dimensional image. The method represents objects using neural radiance fields and searches for viewpoints that cause classifiers to make mistakes.

Instead of producing only one problematic viewpoint, ViewFool characterizes a diverse distribution of them using an entropy-based regularizer. This helps accommodate fluctuations in camera pose and reduce the mismatch between physical objects and their neural representations. Experiments report strong classifier vulnerability and high transferability of the discovered viewpoints across models.

The authors also introduce ImageNet-V as a benchmark for viewpoint robustness. Testing 40 classifiers with varied architectures, training objectives, and augmentations reveals substantial performance drops. These results establish viewpoint change as an important challenge in the evaluated models. They also suggest that ViewFool could supply useful training augmentation, although the abstract presents improved robustness through that route as a possibility.
neurips-2022-viewfool-evaluating-the-rob.tldr: ViewFool finds transferable adversarial camera viewpoints and introduces a benchmark exposing substantial viewpoint sensitivity across 40 classifiers.
